title: 2-D grid-coordinate (physical-layout) selector sweep
hypothesis: K4's alphabet selector is keyed on a 2-D grid coordinate (row/col/boustrophedon, reduced or raw) from the engraving layout, at some width W
best_partial: 0 full-crib-determined grid selectors (reduced+raw) at any width 7-31; 81 under-determined, 63 raw-proper but degenerate
insights: Swept widths W in [7,31] x grid selectors x 3 alphabets x 3 conventions. Selector families: 450 REDUCED instances (row/col/diag/boustrophedon mod 2/3/4) and 125 RAW instances (un-reduced per-row/column polyalphabetic).

OPERATIVE BAR = crib-determined AND full (every 97-position class crib-pinned) AND English. Crib-determined fits (some alpha/conv): 81; of those, 0 are FULL (decryptable) and 81 are crib-UNDER-determined (a position lands in a crib-free class -> free rotation = the exp-059 degeneracy). English decrypts (free-hex > -16): NONE.
No grid selector (reduced OR raw) is full-crib-determined; none decrypts.

PROPERNESS (context, not the bar): reduced selectors that properly 3-colour the crib graph: 0/450 (a real structural obstruction -- arithmetic-progression grid selectors do not separate the conflict graph); raw selectors: 63/125 are proper (high class-count colours for free) BUT are crib-under-determined, so properness buys no decrypt.

VERDICT: across all widths 7-31, NO 2-D grid-coordinate selector -- reduced (mod 2/3/4) or raw (per-row/column polyalphabetic), in row/col/diagonal/boustrophedon form -- is simultaneously crib-determined, full, and English-decrypting. Reduced selectors fail at properness (structural); raw selectors are proper but crib-under-determined (degenerate). The physical-layout 'clock' axis is closed. The remaining open move is a NEW K1-K3 ciphertext invariant (exp 091).
next_steps: 2-D physical-clock axis closed across widths 7-31 (reduced + raw); build the K1-K3 invariant-mining forward filter (exp 091)
